name: Terracotta rainscreen
summary: A modern wall skin of extruded, hollow terracotta panels that hang on rails with an air gap behind them. The clay face is matt, flat and in earth colours, with a thin glaze or an engobe.

philosophy.core_thesis: A wall of fired clay can be a light, ventilated skin: the panel keeps the rain from the insulation, and the air behind it dries the wall.
design_principles: Extrude the panel hollow in a die; the wall of the panel is 15 to 30 mm thick.
Hang each panel on a rail of stainless steel or aluminium, with an air gap of 20 to 50 mm.
Keep the joint open, 6 to 10 mm, so that the wall can drain and dry.
Use a matt face in earth colours: red, brown, buff, grey and white.
Make the panel in a width of 300 to 600 mm and a length up to 1.5 m, to match the grid of the building.
Fire the panel once; the engobe or the glaze fires together with the body.
Use baguettes or fins for a facade with depth and shadow.
anti_patterns: A thick, solid terracotta block laid in mortar
A glossy, mirror-like glaze on the panel
A closed joint with no air gap

form.shape: Hollow, extruded panels, flat or with a profile; baguettes, fins, louvres and tile planks that hang in a regular grid.
form.profile: A flat or lightly ribbed face with a sharp edge; the panel section is a hollow rectangle with webs and a groove for the clip.
form.foot_and_rim: The top and bottom edges have grooves for a rail clip; the sides are square and open at the joint, with a small drip edge.
form.proportion: A panel is about 300 to 600 mm wide, 600 to 1500 mm long and 30 to 40 mm deep; the wall is 15 to 30 mm thick.
rules: Make the panel hollow and extruded.
Hang it on a rail with an air gap.
Keep the joint open and straight.
Use a matt face and one earth colour for the wall.

bodies.rule: Use a dense, pure terracotta clay with fine grain, so that the extruded panel fires true and stays flat. Keep the colour even in each batch.

methods: single firing with the glaze or engobe
forming.joins: Each panel hangs on a clip and rail of stainless steel; no mortar binds the panels, and the joint stays open for drainage.
forming.details: A fine ribbed back, a groove for the clip, a very sharp edge and a slight colour change from one firing to the next.

glaze.pattern: Plain fields of one colour in a regular grid; some panels carry a fine groove, a baguette profile or a printed image in a ceramic ink.
glaze.gloss: Matt to satin, about 5 to 35 GU; the face reflects little light and shows the grain of the clay.
glaze.wear: The panel keeps its colour and shape for decades; a dirty film washes off in rain, and a damaged panel can be swapped.

palette.strategy: Earth colours in clean fields: red, brown, buff, grey and white, with a matt face; the facade gets variety from the grid, the depth and the shadow.

firing.kiln: A roller or tunnel kiln with a controlled curve; the panels run through in one firing, and the heat is the same for each load.
processes: extrusion and drying of the panel
application of an engobe or a glaze
firing.scale: Factories in Germany and elsewhere make panels by the thousand square metres; a single building can use more than 5,000 m².
firing.signs: A ribbed back, a rail groove at the edge and an open joint with a shadow.

pieces.form: Extruded flat panel in terracotta red with a hidden clip groove
Baguette fin with a round section for a deep, shadowed facade
Long glazed plank in a pale satin for a bay of a facade
Panel with a digital print of a leaf in ceramic ink

emotion.target_response: Calm and care: the viewer sees a quiet, earthy wall with a fine grid that shows its craft in the shadow.

use_cases: a render of a modern building with a clay facade
a detail drawing of a ventilated terracotta wall
a facade material brief with an earth colour
avoid_when: the brief needs a shiny, ornamental facade
the brief needs a mortar-bound brick wall
the brief needs a handmade, irregular surface

modifiers.how: Add a high-gloss glaze in blue-green, a gold band and a zigzag in low relief.
Change to thick pressed blocks with deep relief and bed them in mortar on a brick wall.

ornament_level.note: Ornament stays low; the grid, the depth and the shadow give the variety.

wall_thickness.note: The panel wall is 15 to 30 mm, with webs inside.
